cwe_assessments.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code demonstrates prototype pollution mechanism: user-controlled property names (key) from forOwn iteration are directly assigned to target object o[key] = value when val is null/undefined, without validation of special property names like '__proto__' or 'constructor'

connection.evidence: User-provided objects are iterated via forOwn (line 18), extracting property names (key) and values (value). When target property is null/undefined (line 20), the user-controlled key is used for direct assignment to target object o[key] = value (line 21)

diff_causality.evidence: The null/undefined check at line 20 is the conditional trigger for the vulnerable assignment. If this check were removed or modified, the assignment behavior would change, affecting when prototype pollution can occur

security_control.evidence: No validation of property names (keys) before assignment to target object
security_control.required_control: Property name validation/sanitization to prevent assignment to special prototype properties
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-1321 requires preventing modification of object prototype attributes through user-controlled property names
existing_controls_checked: No key validation before o[key] assignment
isObject check only applies to nested object merging, not property name validation
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The code directly assigns o[key] = value without checking if key is a dangerous prototype property like '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype'

concrete_impact.evidence: Assignment to prototype properties can modify Object.prototype, affecting all objects in the application and potentially leading to denial of service, remote code execution, or privilege escalation depending on downstream usage

cwe_assessments.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted or modified to include property name validation, prototype pollution through special property names would be prevented
supporting_evidence: forOwn iterates over object properties including inherited ones (line 18)
Direct assignment o[key] = value occurs when target property is null/undefined (lines 20-21)
No validation of property names before assignment to target object
User-controlled objects are processed through the function (objects parameter)
unresolved_facts: Whether for-own library filters out prototype properties by default
Real-world usage patterns and input validation in calling code
cwe_assessments.review_comment: The defaults function assigns user-controlled property names directly to the target object without validating for dangerous prototype properties. When the target property is null or undefined, the function assigns the value using the unvalidated key, allowing potential modification of Object.prototype if keys like '__proto__' are provided. Add property name validation to reject or escape special prototype property names before assignment.
